active_inquiry.handoff_conclusion: M2 observed the compiled arm with two enabled gear-5 actuators, 2 ms Euler physics, a 20 ms visible control interval, zero gravity, explicit damping and armature, compiled link masses near 0.099 kg and 0.052 kg, and generalized shoulder/elbow inertias near 0.010--0.012 kg*m^2. It also observed the contractual reset at 22 cm with a rank-1 endpoint Jacobian, feasible inverse branches for every sampled target on the 6--20 cm grid, full-rank branch solutions away from reset, and substantial but potentially overshooting response to a one-interval unit action. These observations weaken static infeasibility and substantially reduce the earlier concern that unknown compiled defaults alone explain the control problem; they do not establish protected-runtime fidelity, learned behavior, or hold success. The consequential competing explanations remain: (A) singularity exit and direct-torque transients cause delayed reach or overshoot; (B) the baseline exposure gap causes failures in the official 6--14 cm inner annulus; and (C) policies reach the target but fail the complete hold through residual endpoint motion. Aggregate reward or minimum distance cannot distinguish them. The inquiry will test a learned artifact from the contractual reset and retain first reach, distance, endpoint-velocity/hold interruption, maximum hold, branch, saturation, and radius/angle diagnostics. request.current_synthesis: Observed in completed M2: the compiled model has two enabled gear-5 actuators, 2 ms Euler physics, a 20 ms visible control interval, zero gravity, explicit 0.5 damping and 0.01 armature, and compiled link masses of about 0.099 kg and 0.052 kg. On a 24-point grid spanning radii 0.06, 0.14, and 0.20 m and eight angles, every target had at least one joint-limit-feasible inverse branch; all 48 branch solutions were full-rank with condition numbers from 1.67 to 5.29, although two individual branch solutions were joint-limit-infeasible. Interpretation: the mechanism is not statically unreachable and has substantial direct-torque authority plus damping, but a one-interval command can move farther than the 1 cm hold ball, making velocity shaping and early capture plausible bottlenecks. Competing explanations remain: (A) a learned policy will mainly fail because the singular launch and direct-torque transient delay or overshoot first reach; (B) the dominant gap will be the visible training exposure mismatch, especially the omitted 6--14 cm inner annulus; (C) first reach will be adequate but residual endpoint motion will interrupt the 100-step hold. M2 supports the physical premises behind A and weakens static-feasibility and unknown-compiled-default explanations, but it does not test a policy, target-conditioned launch, closed-loop settling, runtime fidelity, or official protected semantics. The unit-action response is open-loop and cannot establish task success or causal failure attribution.
